data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts following an explicit checklist is more reliable than a single expert because it replaces a single point of failure (the expert's cognitive bias/fatigue) with a redundant, distributed verification system that minimizes 'type 1' errors.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires 'synthetic' judgment where the whole is greater than the sum of the checklist parts.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is poorly designed, introducing new systemic biases that override the benefit of redundancy.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist decomposes a complex intuitive leap into a series of binary, verifiable sub-tasks.
